title: Measuring Verifier Impact in an LLM Generate→Verify→Repair Loop for Intent→Configuration NetOps Tasks
abstract: We measure how inserting a deterministic network verifier into a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) loop affects verifier-detected safety violations for LLM-produced device-configuration proposals. In a preregistered paired design (N = 500 intent→configuration tasks stratified across VLAN-change, ACL-change, and static-route-change clusters) we compared: (1) baseline — a single LLM proposal produced once per task, and (2) guarded — the identical shared LLM proposal validated by a deterministic netops verifier and subjected to up to one automated repair iteration if the verifier flagged a preregistered high/medium-severity violation. Primary outcome: verifier pass (no preregistered high/medium-severity violations). Results (complete pairs = 500): baseline passed 499/500 (0.998), guarded passed 500/500 (1.000); contingency: n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). The preregistered exact McNemar two-sided test was implemented as an exact binomial on discordant pairs (n = n10 + n01); with n = 1 and n10 = 1 the archived two-sided p = 1.00 under that convention. Interpretation: on this verifier-scoped synthetic corpus and model+validator pairing the LLM produced near-ceiling proposals; marginal verifier+repair effect on the pass-rate metric is therefore small, though the verifier corrected at least one concrete baseline failure. All preregistration, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call traces, execution logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being applied to NetOps tasks such as translation of operator intent to device configuration, multi-step change planning, and programmatic repairs. System reports and surveys emphasize that operational safety depends heavily on surrounding engineering: deterministic validators, sandbox replay, canarying, and rollback mechanisms [Beckett et al., 2017; Wei et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. A widely proposed operational pattern is generate→verify→repair (G→V→R): an LLM generates a candidate configuration, a deterministic verifier checks a set of formalized properties, and automated or human-in-the-loop repairs are applied for violations.

Despite conceptual consensus, controlled measurements that isolate the marginal contribution of a verifier (holding the model’s proposal fixed) are scarce. Practitioners must know: when an LLM already produces high-quality candidates over verifier-modelled properties, how much incremental safety does a verifier plus a modest automated repair budget provide on a verifier-scoped pass/fail metric? To answer this precisely we preregistered and executed a paired experiment that isolates verifier+repair impact under canonical, deterministic semantics. Our objective is intentionally narrow and operational: given identical initial proposals (shared-initial_candidate semantics), how much does integrating a deterministic verifier and at most one automated repair iteration reduce verifier-detected safety violations compared to the same LLM alone?
sections.related_work:
Deterministic and formal network configuration verifiers (header-space analyses, route-model checkers, Batfish-style analyzers) can check properties such as reachability, isolation, and update atomicity and have been widely used to increase NetOps assurance [Beckett et al., 2017]. Recent NetOps/AIOps systems integrate LLMs for intent parsing and configuration generation while emphasizing guardrails (validators, sandboxes, rollback) to manage operational risk [INTA, 2025; Wang et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. Generate–verify–repair and verifier-in-the-loop designs are proposed across structured-generation domains to reduce unsafe outputs [PoeTone; INTA].

Complementary literature documents LLM-driven failure modes (hallucination, overconfidence, tool-integration errors) and recommends verification or human oversight as mitigations [Owen, 2026; DeepSeek-AI, 2025]. What is less prevalent in the supplied evidence is a controlled preregistered ablation that quantifies the marginal verifier effect while keeping the LLM’s initial output identical for both arms. This work contributes such an artifact-backed measurement and situates it among those system and verification studies.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. We preregistered study_id cand_7f4b9a2d_hosted_gvr_v1_2026 and froze the research question, task-generation seeds, estimands, inclusion/exclusion rules, analysis executor, multiplicity plan, retry policy, and stopping rule prior to observing results. Primary confirmatory hypothesis: an LLM paired with a deterministic verifier plus a single automated repair iteration will produce a lower verifier-detected safety-violation rate than the same LLM producing a single proposal without verifier feedback (paired, within-task). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline where success == verifier reports zero preregistered high/medium-severity violations. The preregistration and the preregistration SHA-256 are archived in the evidence bundle (see execution manifest).

Task corpus. A deterministic synthetic generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) produced N = 500 intent→configuration tasks with preregistered seeds and stratification into three clusters: VLAN-change (167), ACL-change (167), and static-route-change (166). Tasks were constrained to verifier-modeled features (allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}) so that the deterministic validator could evaluate every candidate within its modeled scope. Replacement/exclusion rules were preregistered; no confirmatory exclusions occurred and complete_pair_count = 500.

Generation semantics and arms. To isolate verifier effect we used generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (independent_condition_generation = false). For each task the pipeline produced a single shared LLM proposal that served as the baseline output; the guarded arm validated that same shared proposal, invoking at most one automated repair call only if the verifier flagged a preregistered high/medium-severity violation on the shared candidate. This design prevents conflation between verifier-guided regeneration and verifier+repair applied to the same proposal.

Models and verifier. The requested LLM was gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json archived). The deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) implemented the scorer-rule full_intent_constraint_validation over a preregistered property set and a mapped severity scale archived in the validator-spec artifacts. The guarded path permitted a single automated repair iteration per the preregistration.

Statistical procedures. The preregistered primary test was an exact McNemar two-sided test on paired binary outcomes. The archived analysis executor implemented the exact McNemar as an exact binomial test on discordant pairs (n = n10 + n01) with two-sided p computed as p_two-sided = 2 × min{P(X ≤ n10), P(X ≥ n10)} for X ∼ Binomial(n, 0.5), truncated at 1.0; this convention is documented in the analysis artifacts. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CIs for the absolute difference were computed with B = 10,000 resamples and bootstrap_seed = 1729. Missingness and retry policies were enforced per preregistration; execution accounting and provider-call traces are archived.
sections.results:
Execution and primary outcomes. The run completed under the adapter contract with complete_pair_count = 500, model_calls_used = 501 (shared_initial_generation = 500; repair-stage calls = 1), and failed_episode_count = 0. Aggregated per-condition counts (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes = 499, baseline failures = 1 (baseline_success_rate = 0.998); guarded successes = 500, guarded failures = 0 (guarded_success_rate = 1.000). Paired contingency (guarded × baseline): n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002.

Exact test and CI. Under the archived exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention the two-sided p = 1.00 for the observed discordant counts (n = 1, n10 = 1). The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute difference is [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). All computations, seeds, and resampling parameters are recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl and analysis/results.json.

Discordant episode: provenance and sanitized summary. The run invoked exactly one repair-stage provider call; that single repair produced the sole discordant outcome (n10 = 1), i.e., the guarded arm converted one baseline-detected violation into a verified pass. The complete per-episode records (validator_trace, repair_provider_trace, normalized configurations, and provider-call trace) for this discordant episode are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl and are reproducibly locatable there. Per the archived validator_trace and repair trace (sanitized for operational sensitivity), the verifier reported a preregistered medium-severity workflow-policy violation on the shared initial proposal that would have violated a modelled group-availability invariant; the automated repair applied by the guarded arm adjusted the proposal sequence to restore the modeled invariant and the verifier subsequently reported no preregistered high/medium-severity violations. The run-level manifests (deterministic_reconciliation.json and provider-call audit) confirm exactly one such repair-stage call and exactly one converted baseline failure → guarded pass. For deterministic audit readers can filter the archived execution/raw_results.jsonl for the single pair entry with baseline pass==0 and guarded pass==1 to retrieve the full archived traces and the exact pair identifier.

Per-cluster realization and power considerations. Realized per-cluster sample sizes matched the preregistered allocation: VLAN-change = 167, ACL-change = 167, static-route-change = 166 (total 500); the per-task generation seeds and cluster assignments are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl. The preregistered power calculation assumed baseline failure prevalence ≈ 0.30; observed baseline failure prevalence was far lower (1/500), producing a ceiling effect and limiting sensitivity to detect small absolute improvements on the composite pass/fail metric. Consequently, secondary per-violation-class analyses were uninformative due to near-zero counts. All missingness and contamination diagnostics (missingness_summary.csv, contamination_summary.csv) show no confirmatory exclusions or flagged contamination.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. Under the constrained regime — single requested LLM (gpt-5-mini), shared_initial_candidate semantics, a deterministic verifier modeling a limited feature set (allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}), and at most one automated repair iteration — the LLM produced near-ceiling correct proposals and the measured marginal pass-rate benefit of adding the verifier was small (0.002). This is a conditional, verifier-scoped measurement: when baseline proposal quality is very high relative to verifier-modeled properties, modest verifier+repair budgets may yield negligible measurable gains on a composite pass/fail metric despite correcting rare concrete failures (as observed).

Design-choice implications. The shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally isolate verifier+repair effect conditional on identical proposals and are representative of deployment semantics that preserve the original human-reviewable candidate and attempt minimal automated repair. Alternative operational semantics—verifier-guided regeneration, multiple repair iterations, or cost-weighted objectives—may yield different trade-offs and should be measured under separate preregistrations.

Threats to validity. Internal validity is supported by preregistration, deterministic seeds, automated replacement rules, and the execution manifest; no manual adjudication occurred. Construct validity is limited by the verifier’s modeled coverage and severity mapping (archived in the validator-spec): pass==no high/medium-severity violations is relative to that coverage. Production-critical properties outside the verifier scope (vendor-specific CLI quirks, dynamic protocol state) are not measured here. External validity is limited by single-model testing (gpt-5-mini requested), synthetic task corpus, and a constrained feature set; results do not imply multi-model or cross-vendor generality.

Statistical nuance. The archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 reflects the executor’s exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs computation for n = 1; such small-n exact p-values can be non-intuitive and are complemented here by a paired-bootstrap CI. The principal takeaway is descriptive: a point-estimate improvement exists (0.002) but inference is constrained by a ceiling effect and the small number of discordant outcomes.

Practical recommendations. (1) Measure baseline proposal error prevalence over verifier-modeled properties on representative operational workloads before allocating repair budgets: extremely low baseline error yields small marginal returns per unit repair effort. (2) Align verifier coverage and severity mappings with operator-critical constraints; expand verifier scope when necessary. (3) Choose generation semantics to match operational priorities: shared-initial semantics conserve model-call budget and preserve the original proposal for human review; verifier-guided regeneration may increase final-pass probability at higher call cost.

Reproducibility. All artifacts required to reconstruct the run are archived in the evidence bundle: preregistration, task generator code and seeds, model_configuration.json, execution/raw_results.jsonl (including the discordant episode traces and pair identifier), execution/task_manifest.jsonl, provider-call traces, validator traces, analysis CSVs, and deterministic_reconciliation.json. Execution accounting recorded model_calls_used = 501 and observed repair-stage calls = 1; these counts reconcile with the archived per-episode records.
sections.conclusion: We performed a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment (N = 500) that isolated the verifier+single-repair effect under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The LLM produced near-ceiling verifier-scoped proposals (baseline 499/500; guarded 500/500), giving an absolute improvement of 0.002 (95% CI [0.0, 0.006]; archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 under the run’s exact-binomial convention). This conditional measurement illustrates a ceiling-effect regime: when baseline proposal quality is very high for verifier-modeled properties and the verifier’s coverage is limited, the measurable marginal pass-rate benefit of a modest verifier+repair budget can be negligible on a composite pass/fail metric, although the verifier can correct rare concrete failures. We recommend measuring baseline error prevalence on representative workloads, aligning verifier coverage with operator-critical properties, and selecting generation/repair semantics that match deployment priorities. The full preregistration, code, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection of every claim made here.

limitations: Synthetic, deterministic task corpus limited to features modeled by the deterministic validator; task payloads constrained to allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}. Results do not generalize to unconstrained production intents, cross-vendor CLI heterogeneity, or protocol semantics outside the verifier scope.
Single requested model family (gpt-5-mini requested) and a single validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) — no claim of multi-model or cross-validator generality is made.
Maximum one automated repair iteration was permitted by the preregistration; different repair budgets or iterative regeneration strategies could change measured verifier impact.

Very high baseline pass rate (499/500) created a ceiling effect that limits power to detect small absolute improvements on the pass-rate metric; the archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 reflects the archived exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention and the small discordant count.

The single discordant episode (the sole task where baseline failed and guarded succeeded) and its validator diagnostics and repair-stage trace are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl in the evidence bundle. To inspect it deterministically: filter execution/raw_results.jsonl for pair entries where the baseline scoring outcome indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass == 0) while the guarded scoring outcome indicates pass == 1; because only one such discordant pair exists in the confirmatory set, this lookup returns the single episode and its provider-call traces. The validator violation-code→severity mapping is archived in the execution manifest and validator-spec artifacts in the bundle.
